subject: Routing a task to OpenAI's GPT-5.5 frontier model versus the Claude tiers

evals.prompt: Define what this skill decides in 2-3 sentences. Distinguish the GPT-5 MODEL-routing decision from the choice of HARNESS that runs GPT.
evals.negative_expectation: Must NOT conflate routing-to-GPT-5 with running Codex, and must not claim GPT-5 is universally best.

evals.prompt: You have four tasks: (a) write a Terraform CI pipeline, (b) re-architect a monolith into services across ~40 files, (c) a security review of an auth diff, (d) a cost-sensitive CRUD feature. Route each to GPT-5, Claude Opus, or Claude Sonnet, and give the per-task reason.
evals.negative_expectation: Must NOT route the cross-system re-architecture to GPT-5 over Opus, and must NOT send the cost-sensitive CRUD work to a frontier tier when Sonnet suffices.

evals.prompt: Correct this claim: 'GPT-5.5 is #1 on SWE-bench Verified, so it's the best coding model — route all coding to it.' Why is the reasoning flawed, and name a concrete coding task where Claude Opus is the better route.
evals.negative_expectation: Must reject 'highest verified score ⇒ route everything to GPT-5'; must cite the narrow margin + contamination caveat AND that Opus leads SWE-bench Pro / complex multi-file resolution.

evals.prompt: For each, say whether `gpt-5-5` owns it or name the skill that does: (a) 'resume my Codex session', (b) 'Opus or Sonnet for this task?', (c) 'GPT-5.5 or Claude for this CI script?', (d) 'which local skill routes payment tasks?'.
evals.negative_expectation: Must route (a) to codex, (b) to claude-opus/claude-sonnet, (d) to skill-router; only (c) is gpt-5-5.

evals.prompt: Why does an explicit GPT-vs-Claude routing rule exist instead of just defaulting to the strongest available model? Reference both task-shape and cost.

Organize GPT-5.5's documented edges and Claude Opus's documented edges into a per-axis routing table (e.g. terminal/CLI work, architecture, multi-file resolution, analytical review, multi-tool coordination). Which axis sends work to which model?
Give an analogy for why you route GPT-5 vs Opus by task type rather than by overall benchmark rank, and why the per-task choice can flip even between two near-equal models.

A teammate routes by headline per-token price ($25 Opus output vs $30 GPT-5 output) and always picks the cheaper one. Explain why that is the wrong routing primitive, including the >272K-token surcharge and the subscription-vs-API billing distinction.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not endorse headline-price routing; must note capability-per-task dominates and that on a subscription the per-token USD is notional, not billed.
